::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How to redefine the \emph command in Beamer?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/13726/how-to-redefine-the-emph-command-in-beamer), asked by [Ulrik Nielsen](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/4294/ulrik-nielsen) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-03-17; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I am using the Beamer class and would like to redefine `\emph` to use `\bfseries` instead of `\itshape`. I have tried the following command:
>
> ```latex
> \renewcommand<>{\emph}[1]{{\only#2{\bfseries}#1}}
> ```
>
> but I get the following error
>
> ```latex
> ! LaTeX Error: Command \beamerx@\emph already defined.
>           Or name \end... illegal, see p.192 of the manual.
> ```
>
> I cannot understand: Why is it a problem that `\emph` already is defined when I am using <code>\<i>re</i>newcommand</code>?
:::

If all you want to do is have `\emph` embolden its text, you could do:

```latex
\let\emph\textbf
```

Each macro is overlay-specification aware and has the same “signature.”  So just alias one for the other.
